stories.headline: Historic flooding swamps the Four Corners, with rooftop rescues and more rain expected through the weekend
stories.summary: Rare, heavy rain that began Wednesday has sent brown floodwaters through parts of New Mexico, Colorado, Utah and Arizona, closing roads and forcing mandatory evacuations and emergency declarations in all four states. In San Juan County, New Mexico, responders pulled people off their roofs as rivers rose to what emergency spokesman Devin Neeley called historic levels, saying “we have not seen flooding like this in generations,” while floodwater pushed sewage into the San Juan River. Farmington’s police chief said no one had died so far but warned “this is not something that should be played with.” In southern Utah, the city of Hurricane declared an emergency after flooding damaged more than 100 homes and RVs, and Colorado Gov. Jared Polis declared disaster emergencies in 11 counties and called up the National Guard for rescues in the southwest of the state. Navajo Nation police said they had rescued seven families, 30 people, from flooded homes, and the Hopi Tribe declared a state of emergency. More rain is expected through the weekend.

stories.headline: An 88-year-old Michigan widow with no internet was credited with 562 ActBlue donations in six weeks, a reporter says
stories.summary: Journalist Charlie LeDuff reported this week that federal records tie Elizabeth Waffle, an 88-year-old widow living in a trailer in Milan, Michigan, to nearly $4,500 in new ActBlue donations over six weeks, 562 transactions in all. Four of them, totaling $22, were logged on the very day LeDuff first visited her trailer, where the power, water and internet are all off; the two tried and failed to make a donation together that day. The new entries included $51 for Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee facing Republican Mike Rogers in a race seen as a possible tipping point for Senate control. Filings reviewed in July had attributed 14,696 donations to her over five years, which LeDuff put at more than $130,000. Waffle said the figures made no sense to her, though she bristled at a possible “hit piece” before agreeing he should keep digging. Not every review agrees: The Center Square found about $100,000 tied to her name across three cycles and noted that ActBlue’s tool for splitting one gift across many campaigns can create multiple logged transactions from a single donation.

stories.headline: Apple posts official do-it-yourself repair manuals for the iPhone Duo on launch day
stories.summary: Hours after the iPhone Duo went on sale Friday, Apple published its official repair manual for the folding phone, with step-by-step instructions for owners and independent technicians replacing individual components, along with detailed diagrams of the internals and lists of the parts and tools each job requires. Separate safety guides cover procedures involving broken glass and battery replacement. Earlier in the day Apple had also posted support documents for software and hardware problems, including hinge issues, Touch ID and display troubleshooting. Apple recommends reading the entire manual before starting and only attempting a repair if you feel comfortable doing it as instructed. Genuine iPhone Duo parts and tools aren’t yet available in Apple’s Self Service Repair Store.

stories.headline: Ex-funeral director who gambled away $1.2 million in prepaid funerals pleads guilty; victims say the deal is too light
stories.summary: Philip Pietras, who once owned funeral homes in Vernon, Coventry, East Windsor and Tolland, pleaded guilty Friday to one count of larceny and four counts of intent to defraud after more than 130 Connecticut residents paid ahead for their funerals and had the money stolen over 16 years. State’s Attorney Craig Nowak said police uncovered more than $1.2 million Pietras had collected on funeral contracts, money the state says went to MGM Springfield, Foxwoods, shopping and even a cruise. Under the deal he will get 15 years, suspended after seven and a half, plus restitution, with sentencing set for January. Victims and their families said the punishment doesn’t fit the crime. “He went on a cruise? How about sending us elderly people on a cruise,” said Sheila Lawlor, and Marguerite Koch said, “You know full well we’ll never get a penny… There is no money.” Pietras has been evicted and lost his embalming license; the state expects to distribute newly appropriated money to victims next summer.

stories.headline: Lawmakers give Elon Musk until Oct. 31 to explain the Starlink slowdown hitting Ukraine’s military
stories.summary: Six Democratic members of Congress led by Rep. Gregory Meeks and Sen. Peter Welch sent Elon Musk a public letter Friday with five questions about restrictions on Starshield, the military version of Starlink, which Ukrainian forces say has been running at limited capacity since mid-October. Speed caps have hampered Kyiv’s ability to defend against Russian jet-powered drones and coordinate strikes, according to the report. The lawmakers argued that because SpaceX’s shares are publicly traded it must disclose material risks, writing that “the revelation that you personally wielded control over a foreign country’s military communications” would raise governance and geopolitical concerns, and gave Musk until Oct. 31 to answer. No one has publicly taken responsibility for the slowdown, though Trump administration officials have pointed at Musk. President Trump, asked about it this week, defended Musk, saying he would “never do anything wrong.”

stories.headline: The 2027 Jeep Wrangler adds standard features, from Alpine audio and a trail camera on Sahara to heated seats on Rubicon
stories.summary: Jeep has released its changes for the 2027 Wrangler, and the Sahara gets the biggest upgrade: the four-door Unlimited Sahara now comes standard with McKinley-trimmed seats, side steps, a nine-speaker Alpine premium audio system, built-in navigation, rear park assist, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-path detection, an auto-dimming mirror, automatic high beams and a garage door opener, plus the front-facing TrailCam for seeing terrain over the hood. Sport, Sport S and Willys models get a 7-inch color instrument display, and Sport S and Willys add passive entry. The two-door Willys gets the vented power dome hood as standard, and Rubicon adds heated front seats, a heated steering wheel and navigation. Engine choices carry over: the 285-horsepower 3.6-liter Pentastar V6 is still offered with a six-speed manual or eight-speed automatic, the turbocharged 2.0-liter four makes 270 horsepower, and the 392 HEMI V8 delivers 470 horsepower. There are more paint colors too; Jeep hasn’t announced pricing.

stories.headline: Mastodon’s Brann Dailor on how Brent Hinds’ death and losing his mother shaped the band’s new album “Marrow Deep”
stories.summary: Mastodon learned that former guitarist and singer Brent Hinds had died in a motorcycle accident at 51 while standing at baggage claim in Alaska for the last date of their 25th-anniversary tour in August 2025, drummer and singer Brann Dailor tells Louder. Hinds had quit the band in acrimonious circumstances five months earlier, and the Alaska State Fair show the next day became a requiem. Dailor said the songs for the new album, “Marrow Deep,” started as a return to the mythological themes of “Blood Mountain” and “Emperor of Sand,” but had already turned personal after his mother Michele died suddenly in February 2025. “I honestly thought… we might actually be able to go back to singing about Pegasus and Bigfoot and the Loch Ness Monster,” he said. “But fate had other plans.” He called the fact that Hinds died before they reconciled “a real gut punch.”

stories.headline: Ridley Scott is producing a new “Alien” movie that picks up from “Prometheus” and “Covenant”
stories.summary: A new “Alien” film is in the works with Ridley Scott producing, according to The Hollywood Reporter, and it is not the long-rumored sequel to 2024’s “Alien: Romulus.” Instead it ties back to “Prometheus” and “Alien: Covenant,” the last two entries Scott directed. Aaron Guzikowski, who worked with Scott on the series “Raised by Wolves,” will write the script, and no director is attached yet. In August Scott told the French outlet AlloCiné that “Romulus” “was OK” but that the franchise “needs some help,” adding, “I’ve already got a footprint for the next Alien… I’m picking up where we left off in Covenant with Michael Fassbender, who now thinks he’s Ozymandias.” THR reports Fassbender isn’t attached yet.

stories.headline: China releases its first fully AI-generated feature film, to weak advance ticket sales
stories.summary: China’s first feature-length film made entirely with AI, a historical fantasy called “Sanxingdui: Future Past,” opened in theaters Friday, but advance ticket sales for the roughly $1.5 million production were weak. The movie is built around the real Sanxingdui dig in Sichuan province, which since 1986 has turned up hundreds of artifacts more than 3,000 years old, including bronze masks with oddly shaped eyes and enormous ears unlike anything else from the era, at the site of a vanished Bronze Age city. Many of the relics were deliberately broken or burned before being buried, a mystery historians often explain as religious offerings at a pilgrimage center that faded around 1000 B.C. The film instead spins a more fanciful, sci-fi explanation for the lost civilization.

stories.headline: France probes a deadly shooting in Trappes as a “terrorist crime” on the eve of Saturday’s protests
stories.summary: A gunman firing from a vehicle in Trappes, west of Paris, killed one person and wounded four others, including a 12-year-old girl, on Friday, and police arrested a 39-year-old man. The shooting was first described as “relatively random,” but Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez later told local media that “the motive may be racist. The investigation is ongoing, but this is clearly a terrorist crime.” The town’s mayor said the dead victim and at least one of the wounded were “of African origin.” The attack comes as France deploys 70,000 police and gendarmes, with helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons, ahead of another weekend of planned protests. President Macron, who canceled a trip to Nigeria and Senegal, blamed last Saturday’s violence on “ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic” and said protests by groups with “no legitimate authority” will be banned. Student union UNEF and the Yellow Vests say they will rally anyway. The Louvre, the Musée d’Orsay and 24 metro stations will close Saturday, and Sunday’s PSG–Lyon match was pushed to Monday, while the Steelers–Saints NFL game at Stade de France is still on.

stories.headline: New Pentagon UFO files describe a silent black triangle that hovered over a ridge, then shot off like a fighter jet
stories.summary: Federal agents guarding an unnamed “national security site” in the western U.S. told the FBI that in June they watched a “substantial, nonreflective, dark black triangular object most resembling a delta wing drone” rise straight up over a ridgeline at dusk, according to documents the Pentagon released Friday. They put its wingspan at nine to fifteen feet. The craft climbed 200 to 300 feet without tilting or wobbling, hovered perfectly still for about 20 seconds, then sped off at a speed “compared to that [of] a military fighter jet,” all in what the Pentagon’s All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office called “absolute acoustic silence.” Through an infrared scope it looked warmer than its surroundings but gave off no exhaust, and a ground search the next morning found no wreckage or disturbance. The 28 files are the seventh batch released under an executive order President Trump signed this year requiring disclosure of sensitive UAP records. AARO said the sighting “warrant[s] further investigation” because it closely matches other reports from federal agents in the West, including orange orbs that released smaller red orbs in 2023.

stories.headline: Hackers jailbreak the iPhone Duo within hours of its launch
stories.summary: Just hours after the iPhone Duo went on sale Friday, hacker team Calif showed one running iOS 27.1 jailbroken, with its icons and widgets bouncing around the screen and an anime character added to the display. Last week the group posted videos of an untethered jailbreak on an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1, which rebooted with root access still available. Calif has not released the jailbreak, and security researcher Stefan Esser told the German site Heise there won’t be a tool for “end users,” though a proof of concept may follow. Esser said the iOS 27.0.1 jailbreak relied on bugs Calif has already disclosed or plans to disclose to Apple soon, and that “most” of them are fixed in the upcoming iOS 27.2 update. He said AI was used to help develop the jailbreak but did not explain how.

stories.headline: Irvine realtor accused of spying on Taiwan’s president’s son for China pleads not guilty; trial set for Nov. 30
stories.summary: Wanying Zhang, a 34-year-old Southern California realtor accused of acting as an agent of China, pleaded not guilty Friday in a Los Angeles federal courtroom, appearing in a white jumpsuit and shackles and speaking only to deny the charge. Prosecutors say she surveilled the son of Taiwan’s president in a Seattle suburb in September 2025 on what they called a spy mission arranged with Chinese intelligence officials. She was arrested earlier this month at LAX while trying to board a flight to China and faces one count of acting as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government. Her husband, Edric Ding, who works with her at the same Irvine real estate firm and had come to earlier hearings, was not there. Prosecutors recently alleged in a filing that Zhang was having an affair with a man who went with her on the Washington trip; CBS identified him as construction entrepreneur Fatai Miao, who has since left for China on a one-way ticket and has not been charged. A pretrial hearing is set for Nov. 12, and the roughly four-day trial is scheduled to begin Nov. 30 in Santa Ana.

stories.headline: Trump lifts 50% tariffs on Canadian boxes, packing gear and seaweed that Maine farmers rely on, a win for Sen. Susan Collins
stories.summary: President Trump on Friday removed 50% tariffs on a handful of Canadian products widely used by Maine’s farms and fisheries, including corrugated boxes, crates, plastic sacks, packing machinery, refrigeration equipment and seaweed, according to a White House proclamation. In exchange, several other Canadian goods were newly hit with 50% duties, among them shampoo, vinyl flooring, coffins, carpets and window air conditioners. Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who is seeking a sixth term in a blue-leaning state, said she had asked administration officials for the relief, which she said protects wild blueberry growers who depend on “specialized harvesting boxes from Canada” as well as apple and potato farmers. “Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense,” she said. Democrats called the carve-outs political; Rep. Richard Neal of Massachusetts said lowering tariffs for a political ally 11 days before the election was a “desperate admission of failed trade policy.”

stories.headline: Tony Iommi says the lost tapes for Black Sabbath’s “Born Again” have turned up, and a remix is “definitely gonna” happen
stories.summary: Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi told Planet Rock’s Ian Danter that he still plans to remix “Born Again,” the band’s 1983 album with Deep Purple singer Ian Gillan and the last Sabbath studio record with drummer Bill Ward. “To be honest, we couldn’t find those tapes for a long time. They disappeared,” Iommi said; they eventually turned up in record company storage, have been transferred and are ready to work on. He admitted many fans have gotten used to the album’s notoriously murky sound and may say a remix isn’t as good, but said the band thought it sounded great in the studio, then heard it on the charts while on tour and wondered, “God, it’s really muffly. What happened?” Gillan himself has called the original mix “outrageous.”

stories.headline: France reports the first known human case of Shamonda, a livestock virus spread by biting midges; the patient died
stories.summary: Health officials in France have reported the first known human infection with Shamonda virus, which normally infects cattle, sheep and goats and is spread by the bites of tiny Culicoides midges. The patient, a Lyon man in his 60s who was already hospitalized for another condition and severely immunocompromised, developed brain-related symptoms and died in early October; officials think he was bitten in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating, and say his weakened health probably contributed to his death. Shamonda, a close relative of the Schmallenberg virus, was discovered in Nigeria in 1965 and had been seen in Africa and Japan before turning up in cattle in southern Germany and Switzerland in June, its first appearance in Europe; it has since spread to other countries, including France. Scientists are still studying how much of a threat it poses to people, but officials say the risk to the general public is likely minimal for now.

stories.headline: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders form a union, believed to be a first among pro sports cheer squads
stories.summary: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have formed a union, and the team has already recognized the bargaining unit, according to a brief joint statement Friday from the Cowboys and the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association, which said the agreement followed “meaningful discussion.” It is believed to be the first union among any pro sports cheerleading squad, apart from a short-lived effort by the Buffalo Bills’ “Buffalo Jills” in the mid-1990s. The next step is negotiating a contract for the 36-member squad, though it isn’t clear how many will be represented. Netflix’s series “America’s Sweethearts” brought new attention to the cheerleaders and helped win them a 400% raise for the 2025 season, with some veterans reportedly earning more than $75 an hour. During the Cowboys’ 1990s heyday they made as little as $15 a game, and a former cheerleader’s lawsuit alleging pay below minimum wage was settled by the team.

stories.headline: A Roman coffin dug up at Westminster Abbey was reused by medieval monks, and researchers think they know for whom
stories.summary: A 4th-century Roman limestone sarcophagus unearthed beside Westminster Abbey more than 200 years ago carries three lines of Latin saying it held one Valerius Amandinus of Roman London, but sometime in the 11th century his body was replaced. The giveaway was its lid, a tapered late Anglo-Saxon slab carved with an early medieval cross. Now carbon dating, a dig through the abbey’s medieval records and a closer study of the coffin have narrowed its later occupant to two 11th-century abbots of Westminster: Ælfwig, who led the monastery from 993 to 1020, and his successor Wulfnoth, abbot until 1049. Abbey archaeologist Warwick Rodwell, writing Tuesday in the Journal of the British Archaeological Association, favors Ælfwig, noting he was already a Westminster monk when elected and “there is no evidence to suggest that he ever left the abbey,” so “there can be little doubt that he was buried in his abbey.”

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday on the Town Hall Green with pumpkin decorating, a live DJ and touch-a-truck
stories.summary: Trumbull’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest runs this Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green at 5866 Main Street, Patch reports. The free family event features pumpkin decorating, face painting, lawn games, crafts and a live DJ, plus a touch-a-truck with the Long Hill Fire and Trumbull Police departments and crafts with the Trumbull Nature and Arts Center. Mobile coffee trailer Brewberry Cafe will serve a seasonal menu.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
